questions.question: A 39-byte SMTP greeting starts at server sequence 7001. What ACK covers it completely?

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.question: How large is the IPv4 packet carrying a 26-byte EHLO payload with 20-byte IP and TCP headers?
questions.explanation: IPv4 Total Length includes its 20-byte header, the 20-byte TCP header, and 26 payload bytes.

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.question: What is the Ethernet MAC-frame length for that 66-byte IP packet, including FCS?
questions.explanation: Add a 14-byte header and 4-byte FCS; 104 includes additional medium overhead and spacing.

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.question: What does TCP port 25 look like as a two-byte network-order hexadecimal value?
questions.explanation: Decimal 25 equals hexadecimal 19; network byte order places the high byte first.

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.question: What is the TCP payload limit for a 1500-byte IP MTU with 20-byte IPv4 and 20-byte TCP headers?
questions.explanation: Subtract both headers from the permitted IP packet size.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.question: Using full 1460-byte payloads whenever possible, how is a 5000-byte stream segmented?
questions.explanation: Three full payloads use 4380 bytes, leaving 620.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.question: Why is splitting the 5000-byte TCP stream into those packets not IPv4 fragmentation?
options: A) The router must add a new SMTP envelope to every fragment
B) TCP creates separate segments before IP encapsulates each one
C) Every packet includes the same IP fragmentation offset
D) Fragmentation and TCP segmentation are the same operation
questions.explanation: Transport segmentation and network-layer fragmentation are different mechanisms.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.question: How long does a signal take to propagate 2000 km at 2 × 10^8 m/s?
questions.explanation: Convert 2000 km to 2000000 m, then divide by propagation speed.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.question: What is the approximate final-acceptance time in the stated 7-RTT plaintext SMTP scenario with RTT 40 ms?
questions.explanation: The example waits for the final TCP handshake ACK to reach the server before the greeting, then counts five SMTP exchange intervals.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.question: Base64 encodes a 3000-byte attachment into how many characters before line wrapping?
questions.explanation: Each three-byte input group produces four characters; line endings and MIME headers are additional.

source.section: Section 14 — Worked examples of size timing and loss

questions.question: B receives a local IPv4 packet with Protocol 6. Which implementation handles the payload next?
options: A) SMTP directly before transport processing
D) An Ethernet switch learning table
questions.explanation: The receiver dispatches the IP payload by protocol and then TCP demultiplexes to the connection.

questions.question: An SMTP 550 recipient rejection arrives after TCP establishment. What is established by this evidence?
options: A) No TCP handshake could have occurred
B) The sender must have the wrong gateway MAC
C) The application exchanged data over the network and reported a recipient or policy failure
D) The packet was rejected by the physical layer
questions.explanation: An application reply proves useful transport communication, even if delivery is rejected.

source.section: Section 15 — Failure analysis and explained cases

questions.question: Why might an endpoint capture show an apparently invalid outgoing TCP checksum?
options: A) Every SMTP client deliberately sends corrupt checksums
B) The DNS TTL expired during Ethernet transmission
C) Checksum offload may leave calculation to the network interface after capture
D) TCP checksums include the next router TTL
questions.explanation: Capture position relative to interface offload affects what is observed.

source.section: Section 12 — Encapsulation and a fully specified packet

questions.question: Small commands succeed but large DATA packets stall with DF set. Which is one plausible diagnosis?
options: A) A proven error in the visible message To field
B) Proof that TCP never completed its handshake
C) A path-MTU mismatch with blocked feedback
D) An Ethernet switch changing the SMTP DATA terminator
questions.explanation: Large packet failure with successful small traffic can suggest a path-MTU problem, but further evidence is needed.

source.section: Section 15 — Failure analysis and explained cases

questions.question: Which statement best describes the final receiving path?
options: A) SMTP parsing, then TCP reordering, then IP addressing
B) The NIC stores the email directly into Bob mailbox without TCP
C) The router removes every protocol header and delivers SMTP bytes to Bob
D) Link validation, IP local delivery, TCP stream reconstruction, then SMTP parsing
questions.explanation: Each layer interprets its own unit before the application processes the reconstructed data.
